title: uswf-1998-heavyweight
label: Mark Williams

won.source: The fed's own Championship Triangle Match broadcast: the ring announcer crowns 'Mark Williams' while the referee raises Chris Williams's hand, after Chris performed the deciding pinfall in his brother's stead.

lost.source: The fed's own first pay-per-view (MAYhem): Bill Vaughn pins Mark Williams for the title.

how: Chris Williams, introduced moments earlier as Mark's identical twin, secretly took his brother's place mid-match and scored the pinfall on Steve Shine; the ring announcer credited Mark Williams regardless.
note: The broadcast itself never resolves whether Mark or Chris actually wrestled the deciding fall; the record credits the belt to Mark Williams per the in-fiction announcement, with Chris Williams named as the reign's other holder.

title: uswf-1998-heavyweight
label: "Critical" Bill Vaughn

won.source: The fed's own first pay-per-view (MAYhem) recap: a mystery masked man interferes on Vaughn's behalf before he pins Mark Williams.

how: Pinned champion Mark Williams with his own finisher, the Critical Mass, after an unidentified masked interloper attacked Chris Williams at ringside.
note: Still champion when this record ends; no further USWF Championship documents survive.

title: uswf-1998-television
label: John McKenzie

won.source: The fed's own TV Title Battle Royal broadcast: McKenzie is the last man standing among the ring's 27 entrants.

lost.source: The same broadcast: moments after being crowned, McKenzie is ambushed by Steve Shine, who had hidden under the ring for the entire match.

how: Won a 27-man battle royal in his own debut match.
note: Held the belt for only minutes before Shine's post-match ambush.

title: uswf-1998-television
label: "Hollywood" Steve Shine

won.source: The fed's own TV Title Battle Royal broadcast: Shine, who was never eliminated because he hid under the ring, ambushes new champion John McKenzie with his finisher and is declared the winner by the ring announcer.

lost.source: The fed's own first pay-per-view (MAYhem): McKenzie pins Shine to reclaim the title.

how: Never entered the battle royal proper; hid under the ring for its entire duration, then clotheslined and eliminated newly-crowned champion John McKenzie after the bell.
note: The announcer's own declaration awarded Shine the title despite his never having been an active, non-eliminated combatant in the battle royal itself.

title: uswf-1998-television
label: John McKenzie

won.source: The fed's own first pay-per-view (MAYhem): McKenzie pins champion Steve Shine after Krystal Powers's interference backfires.

how: Pinned champion Steve Shine with his finisher, the Detonation, after Shine's own manager Krystal Powers's interference was turned against him.
note: Still champion when this record ends; no further USWF Television Championship documents survive.

title: uswf-1998-tagteam
label: Rail Road Express

won.source: The fed's own first pay-per-view (MAYhem): Freight pins Mars for the fed's first Tag Team Championship after a ringside brawl involving a surprise ally, Subway.

how: Defeated The Gods (Mars and Apollo) with their finisher, the Runaway Train, in the fed's own first Tag Team Championship match; the surprise involvement of a third wrestler, Subway, immediately afterward formed the stable Revolution Zero.
note: The fed's own first and, per the surviving record, only Tag Team Championship reign; still champions when this record ends.
